chapter_title: Chương 303: 0305 [Món quà cuối cùng cũng đến]

segments.title: Chương 303: 0305 [Món quà cuối cùng cũng đến]
segments.content:
Li Yanhong and Zhang Chaoyang, this pair of arch-rivals, the former had just quietened down, while the latter was stirring up a major commotion again.

"President Chen, Sina just called. They're asking if we want to join the 'Olympic Reporting Alliance'."

"The what now?"

"Half a month ago, Sohu signed with 15 mainstream traditional media outlets, announcing the formation of the 'National Olympic Media Alliance'. This alliance Sohu created excludes all other websites, making them the exclusive partner for traditional media. It has provoked the ire of the entire internet industry."

"How did he pull that off?"

"Sohu spent at least 160 million yuan to become the exclusive internet sponsor for the 2008 Olympics. Not only are they responsible for building the official Olympic website, but they also have the exclusive commercial rights to use the five rings and the emblem online. Sohu gets priority for interview slots, priority access to event information from the Olympic Organizing Committee, and priority contact with the Chinese Olympic delegation. They also have 300 passes for unrestricted access to competition venues..."

"What's in it for us if we join Sina's Olympic Reporting Alliance?"

"The Olympic Reporting Alliance is an anti-Sohu alliance initiated by portal websites, led by Sina. When reporting on Olympic events, allies can share information, press releases, and photos with each other. For those with news operations, the entire alliance can share resources and collectively bargain for advertising on the Olympic special coverage pages."

"None of that has anything to do with us."

"Refuse them. We're not getting involved. As for reprinting content, I'd rather just reprint information directly from the official Olympic website."

"Alright, I'll go reply to them then."

How interesting. Last year, the major websites banded together to condemn Baidu; this year, they were forming an alliance to oppose Sohu.

And ironically, Sohu was the leader of the pack that besieged Baidu last year.

Xiaonei and Hainei weren't getting involved, and neither was Tianya Forum. Joining or not joining would have little impact on their interests.

But Chen Guiliang was not about to sit out the grand event of the Olympics.

During the Olympics next year, Xiaonei and Hainei would hold events to encourage users. For users who ranked in the top twenty in terms of popularity, the top prize would be the right to use a small car (to circumvent legal risks), and the lowest prize would be a thousand-yuan mobile phone.

Besides, one didn't necessarily have to be at the Olympic venues.

They could report on Olympic volunteers, or record themselves doing sports at home. As long as it was related to the Olympics or sports, it would count.

Chen Guiliang wasn't joining, but plenty of others were.

Sina was still secretly rallying support, and the news would be announced in another two or three months.

The final alliance members would include: Sina, NetEase, Tencent, TOM Online, sports.cn, Yesky, Yahoo! China, Hexun, JRJ, MSN, China.com, KongZhong, iFeng... as well as numerous regional portals like Eastday and 21CN.

The momentum was tremendous!

But even with so many websites combined, they still couldn't beat Sohu. That nearly 200 million yuan Olympic sponsorship fee wasn't spent for nothing.

Zhang Chaoyang, taking advantage of the opportunity to report on the Olympics, made an absolute fortune in advertising revenue.

The period during and around the Olympics was the highlight of Zhang Chaoyang's life. Countless individuals and organizations extended goodwill to him, actively seeking to build connections and discuss collaborations, as if he had already become the king of the Chinese internet.

It was also from that point on that he completely let it go to his head, and he started partying even harder with celebrities from the entertainment circle.

Chen Guiliang opened portal websites like Sina, NetEase, and Tencent, and discovered they were already building momentum for the formation of the anti-Sohu alliance.

Sina published an article titled "Who is Desecrating the Olympics?", which was reposted by NetEase, Tencent, and many other websites, questioning whether there should be any exclusive online advertising rights for the Olympics.

Chen Guiliang would rather get involved with People's Daily Online's "One Class for All Students" than participate in this nonsense.

He switched the webpage back to the Xiaonei special feature, which was currently providing a live text and image broadcast of "Students Attending the Same Class."

This event was jointly organized by the Beijing Municipal Education Commission and People's Daily Online, and was originally limited to major universities in Beijing.

But when Xiaonei got wind of it, it jumped in as well, launching a nationwide live text and image broadcast and expanding the scope from university students to middle school students.

As a result, the organizers upgraded the event too.

A total of 12 lectures on Party history were held, all taught by top-tier experts.

Xiaonei not only provided a live broadcast but also selected some interesting user questions to send over to the classroom for the experts to answer.

The vast majority of university and middle school students weren't interested in this stuff, but there were still tens of thousands of students watching the live broadcast on Xiaonei.

Chen Guiliang casually promoted the figure to over a hundred thousand.

This data greatly pleased the organizers.

Another half month later, a leader from the Civilization Office even led a team to Bytedance for an inspection tour.

"That online mass lecture you all are doing is excellent," the leader from the Civilization Office praised. "The comrades from the Propaganda Department have also commended it. The rectification of the online environment has now entered a critical stage, and this online mass lecture is something that can definitely be promoted."

Chen Guiliang suggested, "We could invite some organizations to participate, to disseminate scientific and cultural knowledge to netizens."

The leader from the Civilization Office asked, "If we want to expand its influence, the content of the online mass lecture needs to be interesting. It would be best if ordinary netizens were also willing to attend."

Chen Guiliang offered an idea, "Many netizens are interested in the Forbidden City, cultural relics, and history, but they don't have the chance to visit the Palace Museum in person. Could we invite experts from the Palace Museum to give lectures on the history and artifacts of the Forbidden City?"

The leader from the Civilization Office's eyes lit up upon hearing this. "That's an excellent idea! I will help you coordinate with the Palace Museum."

People's Daily Online was definitely going to be involved.

Qianlong.com would probably participate too, as it was a key municipal news website in Beijing.

If Sohu heard about this, they would likely want a piece of the pie as well.

Because organizing such an event could not only increase website activity but also strengthen ties with government departments.

If Chen Guiliang had to rely solely on himself, he would never be able to invite experts from the Palace Museum to give lectures.

Sure enough, just a few days later, Qianlong.com and Sohu officially joined. People's Daily Online and Beijing Daily Group also sent people to help push the initiative forward.

In the end, even Sina and NetEase showed up.

So many people here to reap the rewards!

But since it was Chen Guiliang who had proposed the idea, there would certainly be rewards.

For instance, Bytedance could be named an "Advanced Unit in Spiritual Civilization Construction" or an "Excellent Online Education Demonstration Base," and Xiaonei and Hainei could be named "China's Excellent Cultural Websites," and so on.

These titles might seem useless, but they could be very helpful at critical moments.

For the past two years, the state had been rectifying the online atmosphere and was in urgent need of establishing a few positive role models. As long as Chen Guiliang cooperated actively, he could get a green light for anything he wanted to do in the future.

If the government had any events, it would also give priority to collaborating with Bytedance.

In the blink of an eye, the weekend arrived. The Palace Museum series of online mass lectures was still in preparation.

Xiaonei and Hainei were only participating in the live text and image broadcast; the specifics of the lectures were not their concern.

Li Jian personally drove over, delivering the record player and the record, explaining with great embarrassment, "That friend from Taiwan, he originally said he would come to the mainland after the Spring Festival. But he got delayed for another month or two because of personal matters."

"It's fine as long as you were able to deliver it." Chen Guiliang had almost forgotten about this.

He had originally intended for it to be a Christmas gift from last year, and now it had been delayed almost until this year's May Day holiday.

The main issue was the scarcity and difficulty of acquiring the record.

Chen Guiliang chatted with Li Jian for a while, then took the record player and record home, setting them up in a dedicated room.

Bian Guanyue hadn't arrived yet, so Chen Guiliang sat there listening by himself.

Chen Guiliang couldn't hear any difference. If he had to make a comment, it was that there was a little bit of subtle noise.

Tone-deaf!

He sat on the sofa, and as he listened, he fell asleep.

He had been a bit tired recently, as the financial compliance process before the IPO was still ongoing. Although Chen Guiliang didn't need to solve the problems himself, he had to be consulted and had to sign off on everything.

When signing, Chen Guiliang couldn't help but ask about things, learning and mastering that knowledge along the way.

The "user behavior analysis" technical team was also about to be formally assembled. They had poached a programmer from Taobao at a high salary. The person was still processing their resignation and would probably arrive in Beijing in a few days.

When Chen Guiliang had free time, he would also use a VPN to log into American websites, personally trying and comparing the differences between Chinese and American Web 2.0 sites.

This was all in preparation for the IPO roadshow.

He had to understand his American counterparts in detail so that he could be targeted and precise during his presentation, highlighting his company's unique advantages.

Sigh, all for the sake of going public.

He could finally rest properly after the company was listed.

The sound of a door closing came from outside, waking Chen Guiliang.

He walked into the living room and saw Bian Guanyue hanging up her schoolbag.

"You said you had a surprise?" Bian Guanyue asked with anticipation.

Chen Guiliang said, "I bought a vinyl record player and a vinyl record. Come and have a listen."

Bian Guanyue curiously followed him into the room. At first, she didn't think much of it, but she became surprised after listening for just a few seconds.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Is there a difference? I can't tell."

Bian Guanyue gathered her words. "How to describe it? The sound is more natural, warmer, and more continuous. Did you buy an original pressing?"

Chen Guiliang asked in confusion, "How come I only hear noise?"

"It's unavoidable for a master disc cut directly from the original master tape to have some noise," Bian Guanyue explained. "The reissues from digitally restored master tapes don't have noise because they've undergone noise reduction. They're cleaner, but they've also lost some of the original dynamics."

Chen Guiliang listened intently, but still couldn't hear any difference.

But after hearing Bian Guanyue's explanation, he seemed to feel that the texture was indeed different.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Go look at the record sleeve."

It was a very plain cardboard sleeve, but Bian Guanyue let out a cry of pleasant surprise. "A Lo Ta-yu autographed edition? This kind of thing is really expensive!"

Chen Guiliang smiled. "It wasn't that expensive. I originally wanted to give it to you as a Christmas gift last year. But this thing was hard to buy, so it got delayed until now."

Bian Guanyue stared at the sleeve, it was hard to tell if it was because of Lo Ta-yu's autograph or because Chen Guiliang had put so much thought into preparing the gift. In any case, she couldn't hide the smile on her face.

"You really don't need to give me such an expensive gift," Bian Guanyue said as she carefully put the record case down. "That stone you gave me, I've kept it in my schoolbag this whole time."

Woman, thy name is hypocrisy!

She was bursting with joy on the inside, it was written all over her face, yet her mouth said she didn't care.

Bian Guanyue carefully surveyed the room. She planned to have a record cabinet custom-made. It would be used exclusively for storing records in the future.

"You sit for a while, I've learned a new specialty dish." Bian Guanyue happily ran to the kitchen, smiling as she walked, and humming a little tune.

Chen Guiliang thought to himself: Does preparing a gift with care really have such a great effect? It seems I was too careless before.

What should I get for Tao Xue another day?
